Anabelian aspects of the outer automorphism groups of the absolute Galois groups of mixed-characteristic local fields

Kaiji Kondo
Abstract

In the present paper, we study the outer automorphism groups of the absolute Galois groups of mixed-characteristic local fields from the point of view of anabelian geometry. In particular, we show that, under certain mild assumptions, the image of the natural homomorphism from the automorphism group of a mixed-characteristic local field to the outer automorphism group of the associated absolute Galois group is not a normal subgroup. Furthermore, we show that, for the absolute Galois group of a mixed-characteristic local field satisfying certain assumptions, there exist a continuous representation and a continuous automorphism of the group such that the former is irreducible, abelian, and crystalline, but the continuous representation obtained as the composite of the former with the latter is not even Hodge-Tate. These results significantly generalize previous works by Hoshi and Nishio. A key observation in obtaining these results is to focus on the analogy between the mapping class groups of topological surfaces and the outer automorphism groups of the absolute Galois groups of mixed-characteristic local fields. To the best of the author’s knowledge, this is the first work applying results from the theory of mapping class groups to the anabelian geometry of mixed-characteristic local fields, going beyond a mere analogy between the two.

Introduction

Let pp be a prime number, kk a finite extension of ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}, and k¯\overline{k} an algebraic closure of kk. We write Gk=defGal⁡(k¯/k)G_{k}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\Gal(\overline{k}/k) for the absolute Galois group of kk determined by the algebraic closure k¯\overline{k} and Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) for the group of outer automorphisms of the group GkG_{k} [or, equivalently, the group of outer continuous automorphisms of the profinite group GkG_{k} — cf. [Hsh3], Proposition 3.3, (i)\rm(\hskip 1.79993pti\hskip 1.79993pt), (ii)\rm(\hskip 0.80002ptii\hskip 0.80002pt)]. In the present paper, we study the outer automorphism group Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) from the point of view of anabelian geometry.

A natural and fundamental question is to what extent various kinds of data concerning a field kk can be recovered from the group GkG_{k}. In particular, traditional approaches in anabelian geometry have focused on the question of whether the functor “taking absolute Galois groups” is fully faithful. Unfortunately, this functor from the groupoid of fields isomorphic to finite extensions of ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p} equipped with algebraic closures to the groupoid of profinite groups is faithful but not full if pp is odd [cf., e.g., the discussion given at the final portion of [N-S-W], chapter Chapter VII, §5]. For example, if pp is an odd prime, and k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is Galois but not abelian, then there exists a pair (k′,k′¯)(k^{\prime},\overline{k^{\prime}}), where k′k^{\prime} is a finite extension of ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}, and k′¯\overline{k^{\prime}} is the algebraic closure of k′k^{\prime}, such that kk and k′k^{\prime} are not isomorphic as fields, but the absolute Galois groups GkG_{k} and Gk′=defGal⁡(k′¯/k′)G_{k^{\prime}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\Gal(\overline{k^{\prime}}/k^{\prime}) are isomorphic as [topological] groups [cf. [Hsh2], Theorem F, (i)\rm(\hskip 1.79993pti\hskip 1.79993pt)].

Write Aut⁡(k)\Aut(k) for the group of automorphisms of the field kk. Then we have a natural injective homomorphism Aut⁡(k)↪Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\hookrightarrow\Out(G_{k}) of groups [cf., e.g., [Hsh3], Proposition 2.1]. In the present paper, let us regard Aut⁡(k)\Aut(k) as a [necessarily finite] subgroup of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) by means of this injective homomorphism:

Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk).\displaystyle\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}).

We refer to the subgroup as a field-theoretic subgroup. Here, we note that it is well-known [cf., e.g., the discussion given at the final portion of [N-S-W], Chapter VII, §5] that [although a similar equality always holds for a finite extension of ℚ\mathbb{Q} by the Neukirch-Uchida theorem — cf., e.g., [N-S-W], Chapter XII, Corollary 12.2.2], in general, the equality Aut⁡(k)=Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)=\Out(G_{k}) does not hold. Thus, we are interested in the difference between Aut⁡(k)\Aut(k) and Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}).

Let us recall that various “ring-theoretic characterizations” of the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) have been studied in works such as [Mzk1], [Mzk2], and [Hsh1].

Theorem A ([Mzk1], [Mzk2], [Hsh1]).

Let α\alpha be an automorphism of the topological group GkG_{k}. Then the following conditions are equivalent:

  1. (1)

    The image of α\alpha by the natural homomorphism Aut⁡(Gk)→Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(G_{k})\to\Out(G_{k}) lies in the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}).

  2. (2)

    For every finite dimensional continuous representation ρ:Gk→GLn⁡(ℚp)\rho\colon G_{k}\to\GL_{n}(\mathbb{Q}_{p}) of GkG_{k} that is Hodge-Tate, the composite Gk→αGk→ρGLn⁡(ℚp)G_{k}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\alpha}}{{\to}}G_{k}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\rho}}{{\to}}\GL_{n}(\mathbb{Q}_{p}) is Hodge-Tate.

  3. (3)

    The automorphism α\alpha is compatible with the filtration on GkG_{k} given by the [positively indexed] higher ramification subgroups in the upper numbering.

  4. (4)

    There exists an automorphism of topological groups [but not necessarily of topological fields] (k¯^)+⟶∼(k¯^)+(\widehat{\overline{k}})_{+}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}(\widehat{\overline{k}})_{+} — where we write k¯^\widehat{\overline{k}} for the pp-adic completion of k¯\overline{k} and (k¯^)+(\widehat{\overline{k}})_{+} for the topological group obtained by forming the underlying additive module of k¯^\widehat{\overline{k}} — that is compatible with the natural action Gk↷k¯^G_{k}\curvearrowright\widehat{\overline{k}} [with respect to α\alpha].

As Theorem A shows, the elements of Aut⁡(k)\Aut(k) are characterized as outer automorphisms that preserve various “ring-theoretic structures and properties” such as the ramification filtration, the Hodge–Tate-ness of continuous pp-adic representations, and the continuous GkG_{k}-module (k¯^)+(\widehat{\overline{k}})_{+}. However, Theorem A does not reveal the difference between Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) and Aut⁡(k)\Aut(k).

As a certain refinement of some observations concerning the implication (2)⇒(1)(2)\Rightarrow(1) of Theorem A, the following theorem was proved in [Hsh4].

Theorem B ([Hsh4]).

Suppose that pp is an odd prime number, and that k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is an abelian extension of even degree dd. Then there exist a ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}-vector space VV of dimension dd, a continuous representation ρ:Gk→Autℚp⁡(V)\rho\colon G_{k}\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}(V) that is irreducible, abelian, and crystalline [hence also Hodge-Tate], and a group automorphism φ:Gk⟶∼Gk\varphi\colon G_{k}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{k} such that ρ∘φ\rho\circ\varphi is not Hodge-Tate.

In the present paper, we generalize this result to the case where the Galois extension k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is not necessarily abelian. That is to say, we obtain the following theorem.

Theorem C.

Suppose that pp is an odd prime number, and that k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a finite Galois extension of even degree dd. Then there exist a ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}-vector space VV of dimension dd, a continuous representation ρ:Gk→Autℚp⁡(V)\rho\colon G_{k}\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}(V) that is irreducible, abelian, and crystalline [hence also Hodge-Tate], and a group automorphism φ:Gk⟶∼Gk\varphi\colon G_{k}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{k} such that ρ∘φ\rho\circ\varphi is not Hodge-Tate.

At the time of writing, it is not clear to the author whether or not a similar assertion to Theorem C in the case where k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a Galois extension of odd degree holds. We will discuss the reason why the proof of Theorem C does not work in the case where the extension k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a Galois extension of odd degree in Remark 1.10.

Here, we review an outline of the proof of Theorem B and recall the technical difficulties to generalize the argument to the situation of Theorem C.

To prove Theorem B, it is important to show that there exists an automorphism φ\varphi of GkG_{k} such that the induced automorphism φ×\varphi^{\times} of k×k^{\times}, which is obtained via the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm, does not preserve the subgroup ℤp×⊂k×\mathbb{Z}_{p}^{\times}\subset k^{\times} of k×k^{\times}. When k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a quadratic extension, we construct such an automorphism of GkG_{k} explicitly by applying the techniques developed in [H-N] [cf. Theorem D below].

When k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a finite abelian extension of even degree, the desired existence reduces to the case where k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a quadratic extension in the following way. If k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a finite abelian extension of even degree, then there exists a quadratic intermediate field k′k^{\prime} of k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} such that

Gk⊂Gk′=defGal⁡(k¯/k′)\displaystyle G_{k}\subset G_{k^{\prime}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\Gal(\overline{k}/k^{\prime})

is a characteristic subgroup [cf. [H-N], Lemma 2.6, (i)\rm(\hskip 1.79993pti\hskip 1.79993pt)]. Thus, we obtain an automorphism φ′\varphi^{\prime} of Gk′G_{k^{\prime}} such that (φ′)×(\varphi^{\prime})^{\times} does not preserve the subgroup ℤp×⊂(k′)×\mathbb{Z}_{p}^{\times}\subset(k^{\prime})^{\times} of (k′)×(k^{\prime})^{\times}. Moreover, the restriction φ\varphi to GkG_{k} of the automorphism φ′\varphi^{\prime} satisfies the desired property.

However, the above problem can no longer be reduced to the quadratic case in the case where k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a Galois extension of even degree that is not abelian. Moreover, the action of Aut⁡(Gk)\Aut(G_{k}) on the ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}-vector space k+k_{+} obtained by forming the underlying additive module of the field kk induced by the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm may be complicated. A large portion of §1 of the present paper is devoted to overcoming this difficulty.

Let us make some preparations to state a key result for the generalization. The following theorem is fundamental in the study of the outer automorphism groups of the absolute Galois groups of mixed-characteristic local fields.

Theorem D ([N-S-W]).

Suppose that pp is an odd prime number, and that k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a finite extension of degree dd and of residue degree ff. Then there exist σ\sigma, τ\tau, x0,…,xd∈Gkx_{0},\ldots,x_{d}\in G_{k}, positive integers ss, tt, an element x0′∈⟨τ,x0⟩¯x_{0}^{\prime}\in\overline{\langle\tau,x_{0}\rangle}, and an element x1′∈⟨σ,τ,x1⟩¯x_{1}^{\prime}\in\overline{\langle\sigma,\tau,x_{1}\rangle}, where “⟨S⟩¯\overline{\langle S\rangle}” denotes the closed subgroup of GkG_{k} topologically generated by SS, such that the following conditions hold:

  1. (1)

    GkG_{k} is presented as the profinite group topologically generated by σ\sigma, τ\tau, x0,…,xd∈Gkx_{0},\ldots,x_{d}\in G_{k} and subject to the relations described in the conditions (3) and (4) below.

  2. (2)

    The wild inertia subgroup PkP_{k} of GkG_{k} is topologically normally generated by x0,…,xdx_{0},\ldots,x_{d}.

  3. (3)

    The elements σ\sigma, τ\tau satisfy the relation σ​τ​σ−1=τpf\sigma\tau\sigma^{-1}=\tau^{p^{f}}.

  4. (4)

    In addition, the generators satisfy one further relation:

    1. (a)

      for even dd,

      σx0σ−1=(x0′)tx1ps[x1,x2][x3,x4]⋯[xd−1,xd];\displaystyle\sigma x_{0}\sigma^{-1}=(x_{0}^{\prime})^{t}x_{1}^{p^{s}}[x_{1},x_{2}][x_{3},x_{4}]\cdots[x_{d-1},x_{d}];
    2. (b)

      for odd dd,

      σx0σ−1=(x0′)tx1ps[x1,x1′][x2,x3]⋯[xd−1,xd].\displaystyle\sigma x_{0}\sigma^{-1}=(x_{0}^{\prime})^{t}x_{1}^{p^{s}}[x_{1},x_{1}^{\prime}][x_{2},x_{3}]\cdots[x_{d-1},x_{d}].

We write k×^\widehat{k^{\times}} for the profinite completion of the multiplicative group of kk and k+k_{+} for the ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}-vector space obtained by forming the underlying additive module of kk. When pp is odd, we fix topological generators σ\sigma, τ\tau, x0,…,xdx_{0},\ldots,x_{d} of GkG_{k} as in Theorem D. Let F:Gk→k+F\colon G_{k}\to k_{+} be the homomorphism obtained as the composite of the natural surjection Gk↠GkabG_{k}\twoheadrightarrow G_{k}^{\ab}, the inverse of the isomorphism induced by the local reciprocity map k×^⟶∼Gkab\widehat{k^{\times}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{k}^{\ab}, the projection k×^↠𝒪k×\widehat{k^{\times}}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times} determined by a choice of a uniformizer of 𝒪k\mathcal{O}_{k}, and the pp-adic logarithm logk:𝒪k×→k+\log_{k}\colon\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times}\to k_{+}. Moreover, if pp is odd, then, for each i∈{1,2,…,d}i\in\{1,2,\ldots,d\}, we write yi∈k+y_{i}\in k_{+} for the image of xix_{i} by the map FF. Note that, when d>1d>1 and pp is odd, the dd elements y1,…,ydy_{1},\ldots,y_{d} form a basis of the ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}-vector space k+k_{+} [cf. [H-N], Lemma 1.2; [H-N], Lemma 1.3; [Hsh3], Proposition 3.11, (iv)\rm(i\hskip-0.80002ptv\hskip-0.59998pt)].

We obtain the following result by considering the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm, together with the “Dehn twists” in Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) [cf., e.g., [Kum], [Grp]]. This result is interesting in its own right and, moreover, plays an important role in the proof of Theorem C.

Theorem E.

Suppose that the finite extension k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is of degree d>1d>1, and that pp is odd. We write Trk/ℚp:k+→(ℚp)+\Tr_{k/\mathbb{Q}_{p}}\colon k_{+}\to(\mathbb{Q}_{p})_{+} for the trace map of the extension k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p}. Then we obtain the following equality of sub-ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}-vector spaces of k+k_{+}:

Ker(Trk/ℚp)={⟨y1,y3,…,yd⟩ℚp​(d:e​v​e​n)⟨y2,y3,…,yd⟩ℚp​(d:o​d​d),\displaystyle\Ker(\Tr_{k/\mathbb{Q}_{p}})=\left\{\begin{aligned} &\langle y_{1},y_{3},\ldots,y_{d}\rangle_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}\ (d:even)\\ &\langle y_{2},y_{3},\ldots,y_{d}\rangle_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}\ (d:odd),\end{aligned}\right.\

where “⟨S⟩ℚp\langle S\rangle_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}” denotes the sub-ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}-vector space of k+k_{+} generated by SS.

We obtain a useful description of the sub-ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}-vector space (ℚp)+⊂k+(\mathbb{Q}_{p})_{+}\subset k_{+} in terms of the basis y1,…,ydy_{1},\ldots,y_{d} by applying Theorem E. This description enables us to apply the techniques developed in [Hsh4] to prove Theorem C, which is the first main result of the present paper.

Here, we note that the generators and relations of GkG_{k} in Theorem D are non-canonical, and that the proof of Theorem D is purely group-theoretic. Moreover, it is non-trivial to relate these generators and relations of GkG_{k} to the ring structure of kk. From this perspective, it is of independent interest the issue of whether or not, under rather mild assumptions such as those in Theorem E, one can obtain a result that directly connects the generators and relations of GkG_{k} in Theorem D with the ring structure of kk.

Next, let us discuss the second main theorem of the present paper. First, we recall that one interesting problem from the perspective of algorithmic anabelian geometry is the issue of whether or not the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) can be recovered functorially and group-theoretically from GkG_{k}. For example, as shown in [Hsh2], Theorem 6.12, under suitable assumptions on kk, the set of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k})-conjugates of the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) can be recovered functorially and group-theoretically.

Theorem F ([Hsh2]).

Suppose that kk is Galois-specifiable [cf. [Hsh2], Definition 6.1]. Then the set of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k})-conjugates of the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is equal to the set of strictly quasi-geometric subgroups of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) [cf. [Hsh2], Definition 6.5, (i), (ii)]. In particular, the set of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k})-conjugates of the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) can be recovered functorially and group-theoretically.

It follows formally that if one can establish a functorial group-theoretic algorithm that recovers the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) from GkG_{k}, then it is necessary that the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is a normal subgroup [cf. Remark 2.20]. However, the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is not necessarily a normal subgroup in general as shown in [Hsh2] and [H-N].

Theorem G ([Hsh2]).

Suppose that pp is an odd prime number, and that k=ℚp​(ζp,pp)k=\mathbb{Q}_{p}(\zeta_{p},\sqrt[p]{p}), where ζp∈k¯\zeta_{p}\in\overline{k} is a primitive pp-th root of unity, and pp∈k¯\sqrt[p]{p}\in\overline{k} is a pp-th root of pp. Then the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is not a normal subgroup.

Theorem H ([H-N]).

Suppose that pp is an odd prime number, and that k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a finite abelian extension of even degree. Then the set of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k})-conjugates of the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is infinite. In particular, the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is not normal, and there exist infinitely many distinct [necessarily finite] subgroups of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) isomorphic to Aut⁡(k)\Aut(k).

Theorem G and Theorem H were proved by different techniques. In the present paper, we prove the non-normality of Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) in a more general form that includes both Theorem G and Theorem H. The following result is the second main theorem of the present paper.

Theorem I.

Suppose that pp is an odd prime number, and that k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a finite Galois extension of degree greater than one. Then the set of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k})-conjugates of the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is infinite. In particular, the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is not normal, and there exist infinitely many distinct [necessarily finite] subgroups of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) isomorphic to Aut⁡(k)\Aut(k).

We apply essentially different arguments to prove Theorem I depending on whether [k:ℚp][k\colon\mathbb{Q}_{p}] is even or odd. Suppose that [k:ℚp][k\colon\mathbb{Q}_{p}] is even. Let φ\varphi be an automorphism of GkG_{k} as in Theorem C. We write φ+\varphi_{+} for the automorphisms, which is induced from φ\varphi by the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm. Suppose that k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a finite Galois extension. It follows from the discussion in §1 that the automorphism φ+\varphi_{+} does not preserve the ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}-subspace (ℚp)+⊂k+(\mathbb{Q}_{p})_{+}\subset k_{+} of k+k_{+}. We prove Theorem I in the case where k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a finite Galois extension of even degree by combining this result with the argument of [H-N].

On the other hand, when k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is of odd degree, since it is not clear to the author whether or not there exists an element of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) that does not preserve the ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}-subspace (ℚp)+⊂k+(\mathbb{Q}_{p})_{+}\subset k_{+}, the same technique cannot be applied. A key observation in the proof of Theorem I in the case where k/ℚpk/\mathbb{Q}_{p} is a finite Galois extension of odd degree greater than one is obtained by focusing on the analogy between Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) and the mapping class group of a surface, as developed in [Kum], [Grp], and related works.

In the present paper, we prove Theorem I by comparing, from the perspective of the natural pp-adic Lie group structures, the image of the “subgroup of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) corresponding to the mapping class group” [cf. Remark 2.16] by the group homomorphism Out⁡(Gk)→Autℚp⁡(k+)\Out(G_{k})\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p}}(k_{+}) induced by the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm of [Hsh3], Proposition 3.11, (iv)\rm(i\hskip-0.80002ptv\hskip-0.59998pt), with the image of ZOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))Z_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)) by the same homomorphism.

Here, we note that the case of even degree can also be proved by the same method as in the odd degree case. However, as discussed above, we instead apply another method, which has the additional advantage of providing explicit elements in Out⁡(Gk)∖NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))\Out(G_{k})\setminus N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)) [cf. Remark 2.21].

Although [Kum] and [Grp] studied certain analogies between the outer automorphism groups of absolute Galois groups of mixed-characteristic local fields and the mapping class groups of topological surfaces, there have been very few results that apply this analogy to objects reflecting the ring structure of kk. In the present paper, some results from the theory of mapping class groups are applied to prove the non-normality of field-theoretic subgroups and to establish nontrivial phenomena concerning pp-adic representations. To the best of the author’s knowledge, this is the first work that applies results from the theory of mapping class groups to the anabelian geometry of mixed-characteristic local fields in a way that goes beyond a mere analogy.

0 Notational conventions

Monoids. In the present paper, every “monoid” is assumed to be commutative. Let MM be a monoid. [The monoid operation of MM will be written multiplicatively]. We shall write MpfM^{\pf} for the perfection of MM [i.e., the monoid obtained by forming the inductive limit of the inductive system of monoids

⋯→M→M→⋯\displaystyle\cdots\to M\to M\to\cdots

given by assigning to each positive integer nn a copy of MM, which we write for InI_{n}, and to each two positive integers nn, mm such that nn divides mm the homomorphism In=M→M=ImI_{n}=M\to M=I_{m} given by multiplication by m/nm/n].

Groups. If GG is a group, and H⊂GH\subset G is a subgroup of GG, then we shall write NG​(H)⊂GN_{G}(H)\subset G for the normalizer of HH in GG. Moreover, we shall write ZG​(H)Z_{G}(H) for the centralizer of HH in GG.

Topological groups. If GG is a topological group, then we shall write GabG^{\ab} for the abelianization of GG [i.e., the quotient of GG by the closure of the commutator subgroup of GG].

Rings. In the present paper, every “ring” is assumed to be unital, associative, and commutative. If RR is a ring, then we shall write R+R_{+} for the underlying additive group of RR and R×⊂RR^{\times}\subset R for the multiplicative group of units of RR.

Mixed-characteristic local fields. We shall refer to a field isomorphic to a finite extension of ℚp\mathbb{Q}_{p}, for some prime number pp, as an MLF. Here, “MLF” is to be understood as an abbreviation for “mixed-characteristic local field”. Let kk be an MLF and k¯\overline{k} an algebraic closure of kk. Then we shall write

Groups of MLF-type. We shall refer to a group isomorphic to the absolute Galois group of an MLF as a group of MLF-type. Let GG be a group of MLF-type. We shall say that a subgroup of GG is open if it is of finite index. It follows from [N-D], Theorem 0.1, and an elementary argument from general topology that the open subgroups of GG determine the structure of a profinite group of GG, and that this topology of GG is a uniquely determined topology of GG that gives rise to a structure of profinite group on GG. In the remainder of the present paper, we equip GG with this profinite group structure. In particular, an arbitrary isomorphism between groups of MLF-type as abstract groups is necessarily an isomorphism of profinite groups.

Moreover, let us recall [cf. [Hsh3], Definition 3.5, Proposition 3.6, Definition 3.10, Proposition 3.11] that there exist functorial group-theoretic algorithms for constructing, from a group of MLF-type GG,

  • •

    a prime number p⁡(G)p(G),

  • •

    positive integers d⁡(G)d(G), f⁡(G)f(G),

  • •

    subgroups P⁡(G)⊂I⁡(G)⊂GP(G)\subset I(G)\subset G of GG,

  • •

    subgroups 𝒪×​(G)⊂k×​(G)⊂Gab\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)\subset k^{\times}(G)\subset G^{\ab}, where we write recG\rec_{G} for the final inclusion k×​(G)⊂Gabk^{\times}(G)\subset G^{\ab}, and

  • •

    a ℚp⁡(G)\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}-vector space k+​(G)k_{+}(G)

which “correspond” to

  • •

    the prime number pkp_{k},

  • •

    the positive integers dkd_{k}, fkf_{k},

  • •

    the subgroups Pk⊂Ik⊂GkP_{k}\subset I_{k}\subset G_{k} of GkG_{k},

  • •

    the subgroups 𝒪k×⊂k×↪reckGkab\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times}\subset k^{\times}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\rec_{k}}}{{\hookrightarrow}}G_{k}^{\ab}, and

  • •

    the ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}-vector space k+k_{+},

respectively.

Moreover, it follows from [Hsh3], Proposition 3.11, (i)\rm(\hskip 1.79993pti\hskip 1.79993pt), (iv)\rm(i\hskip-0.80002ptv\hskip-0.59998pt); [H-N], Lemma 1.2, that we have natural homomorphisms

Aut⁡(G)→Aut⁡(k×​(G)),Aut⁡(G)→Autℚp⁡(G)⁡(k+​(G)).\displaystyle\Aut(G)\to\Aut(k^{\times}(G)),\ \ \ \Aut(G)\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}}(k_{+}(G)).

Since the automorphism of GabG^{\ab} induced by an inner automorphism of GG is trivial, it follows from the constructions of k×​(G)k^{\times}(G) and k+​(G)k_{+}(G) that the automorphisms of k×​(G)k^{\times}(G) and k+​(G)k_{+}(G) induced by an inner automorphism of GG are trivial. Thus, the above two homomorphisms determine group homomorphisms

Out⁡(G)→Aut⁡(k×​(G)),Out⁡(G)→Autℚp⁡(G)⁡(k+​(G)).\displaystyle\Out(G)\to\Aut(k^{\times}(G)),\ \ \ \Out(G)\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}}(k_{+}(G)).

Let α\alpha be an element of Out⁡(G)\Out(G). We write α×\alpha^{\times} [respectively, α+\alpha_{+}] for the image of α\alpha by the homomorphism Out⁡(G)→Aut⁡(k×​(G))\Out(G)\to\Aut(k^{\times}(G)) [respectively, Out⁡(G)→Autℚp⁡(G)⁡(k+​(G))\Out(G)\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}}(k_{+}(G))]. In the present paper, we call α×\alpha^{\times} and α+\alpha_{+} the automorphisms induced from α\alpha by the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithms.

Let kk be an MLF and α\alpha an element of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}). [Hsh3], Proposition 3.11, (i)\rm(\hskip 1.79993pti\hskip 1.79993pt), (iv)\rm(i\hskip-0.80002ptv\hskip-0.59998pt)].

1 A group-theoretic description of the kernels of absolute trace maps and the application to the study of Aut-intrinsic Hodge-Tate representations

In the present §1, let kk be an MLF, k¯\overline{k} an algebraic closure of kk, and GG a group of MLF-type. In the present §1, we show that the kernel of the trace map for the extension k/k(d=1)k/k^{(d=1)} can be described “group-theoretically”. Moreover, by means of this group-theoretic description of the kernel of the trace map for k/k(d=1)k/k^{(d=1)}, together with classical techniques from pp-adic representation theory, we show that if pkp_{k} is odd, dkd_{k} is even, and kk is an absolutely Galois MLF, i.e., if k/k(d=1)k/k^{(d=1)} is a Galois extension, then there exist a ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}-vector space VV of dimension dkd_{k}, a continuous representation ρ:Gk→Autℚpk⁡(V)\rho\colon G_{k}\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(V) that is irreducible, abelian, and crystalline [hence also Hodge-Tate], and a group automorphism φ:Gk⟶∼Gk\varphi\colon G_{k}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{k} such that ρ∘φ\rho\circ\varphi is not Hodge-Tate. This result generalizes the main theorem of [Hsh4].

Theorem 1.1 (Jannsen-Wingberg).

With the above preparations in place, we can now prove the following assertion, which is the most technically substantial result of the present paper:

This completes the proof of assertion (b).

Next, we prove assertion (c). Suppose that ci≠0c_{i}\neq 0. Then it follows from assertion (b) that y2​i+1,y2​i+2∈Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1))y_{2i+1},\ y_{2i+2}\in\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}). Moreover, it follows from the definition of the map Out⁡(Gk)→Autℚpk⁡(k+)\Out(G_{k})\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(k_{+}) that the following equality holds:

(φi′′)+​(v)−v=(ci+1−ci)​(y2​i+2−y2​i+4).\displaystyle(\varphi^{\prime\prime}_{i})_{+}(v)-v=(c_{i+1}-c_{i})(y_{2i+2}-y_{2i+4}).

Therefore, it follows from Lemma 1.2 that we obtain that

y2​i+4=(φi′′)+​(y2​i+1)−y2​i+1+y2​i+2∈Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1)).\displaystyle y_{2i+4}=(\varphi^{\prime\prime}_{i})_{+}(y_{2i+1})-y_{2i+1}+y_{2i+2}\in\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}).

Consequently, it follows from assertion (a) that y2​i+3∈Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1))y_{2i+3}\in\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}). This completes the proof of assertion (c).

Next, we prove assertion (d). Suppose that ci+1≠0c_{i+1}\neq 0. Then it follows from assertion (b) that y2​i+3,y2​i+4∈Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1))y_{2i+3},\ y_{2i+4}\in\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}). Moreover, it follows from the definition of the map Out⁡(Gk)→Autℚpk⁡(k+)\Out(G_{k})\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(k_{+}) that the following equality holds:

(φi′′)+​(v)−v=(ci+1−ci)​(y2​i+2−y2​i+4).\displaystyle(\varphi^{\prime\prime}_{i})_{+}(v)-v=(c_{i+1}-c_{i})(y_{2i+2}-y_{2i+4}).

Therefore, it follows from Lemma 1.2 that we obtain that

y2​i+2=−(φi′′)+​(y2​i+3)+y2​i+3+y2​i+4∈Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1)).\displaystyle y_{2i+2}=-(\varphi^{\prime\prime}_{i})_{+}(y_{2i+3})+y_{2i+3}+y_{2i+4}\in\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}).

Consequently, it follows from assertion (a) that y2​i+1∈Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1))y_{2i+1}\in\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}). This completes the proof of assertion (d).

We now return to the proof of Theorem 1.3 in the case where dkd_{k} is even. Since dimKer⁡(Trk/k(d=1))=dk−1≥3\dim\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}})=d_{k}-1\geq 3 [cf. the assumption that dk≥3d_{k}\geq 3 and dkd_{k} is even], it follows that there exists some 1≤i≤g1\leq i\leq g such that either ci≠0c_{i}\neq 0 or ei≠0e_{i}\neq 0. It follows from the above claim by a sort of induction that we have y3,…,ydk∈Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1))y_{3},\ldots,y_{d_{k}}\in\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}).

We extend the linearly independent system {y3,…,ydk}\{y_{3},\ldots,y_{d_{k}}\} to a basis {y3,…,ydk,w}\{y_{3},\ldots,y_{d_{k}},w\} of Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1))\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}) over ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}. We may take ww as of the form α1​y1+α2​y2\alpha_{1}y_{1}+\alpha_{2}y_{2} where α1,α2∈ℚpk\alpha_{1},\alpha_{2}\in\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}. If α2=0\alpha_{2}=0, then there is nothing to prove. Suppose that α2≠0\alpha_{2}\neq 0. Let φ\varphi denote the automorphism of GkG_{k} defined similarly to “φ\varphi” that appears in the proof of the case dk=2d_{k}=2. Then it follows from Lemma 1.2 and the definition of the map Out⁡(Gk)→Autℚpk⁡(k+)\Out(G_{k})\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(k_{+}) that the following equality holds:

α2​y1=φ+​(α1​y1+α2​y2)−(α1​y1+α2​y2)∈Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1)).\displaystyle\alpha_{2}y_{1}=\varphi_{+}(\alpha_{1}y_{1}+\alpha_{2}y_{2})-(\alpha_{1}y_{1}+\alpha_{2}y_{2})\in\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}).

This completes the proof of the case where dkd_{k} is even.

  1. (2)

    The case where dkd_{k} is odd.

In this case, by applying a similar argument to the argument applied in (1), we obtain y2,…,ydk∈Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1))y_{2},\ldots,y_{d_{k}}\in\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}). This completes the proof of Theorem 1.3. ∎

Remark 1.4.

In traditional algorithmic anabelian geometry, non-canonical objects such as generators and relations have not played significant roles. In contrast, Theorem 1.3—by fully exploiting generators and relations in addition to conventional methods—establishes a nontrivial connection between these generators and relations and the ring structure of kk. For these reasons, Theorem 1.3 is meaningful in its own right.

Lemma 1.5.

Suppose that pkp_{k} is odd, and that dkd_{k} is even. Let φ\varphi be the automorphism of GkG_{k} defined by the following equalities [cf. Theorem 1.1]:

φ⁡(σ)=σ,φ⁡(τ)=τ,φ⁡(x2)=x2​x1,φ⁡(xi)=xi​(i≠2).\displaystyle\varphi(\sigma)=\sigma,\ \varphi(\tau)=\tau,\ \varphi(x_{2})=x_{2}x_{1},\ \varphi(x_{i})=x_{i}\ (i\neq 2).

Then the following assertions hold:

  1. (1)

    For all n∈ℤ∖{0}n\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}, it holds that φ+n​(k+(d=1))≠k+(d=1)\varphi^{n}_{+}(k^{(d=1)}_{+})\neq k^{(d=1)}_{+}.

  2. (2)

    The intersection φ×​(𝒪k(d=1)×)∩𝒪k(d=1)×\varphi^{\times}(\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times})\cap\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times} is not open in 𝒪k(d=1)×\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}

Proof.

First, we verify assertion (1). Since dkd_{k} is even, it follows from Theorem 1.3 that Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1))=⟨y1,y3,…,ydk⟩ℚpk\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}})=\langle y_{1},y_{3},\ldots,y_{d_{k}}\rangle_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}. Moreover, since k+(d=1)k^{(d=1)}_{+} is torsion-free, and Trk/k(d=1)⁡(x)=dk​x\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}}(x)=d_{k}x for any x∈k+(d=1)x\in k^{(d=1)}_{+}, it follows that

Ker⁡(Trk/k(d=1))∩k+(d=1)=0.\displaystyle\Ker(\Tr_{k/k^{(d=1)}})\cap k^{(d=1)}_{+}=0.

Thus, the 1-dimensional sub-ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}-vector space k+(d=1)k^{(d=1)}_{+} has a basis consisting of an element of the form α1​y1+y2+α3​y3+⋯+αdk​ydk\alpha_{1}y_{1}+y_{2}+\alpha_{3}y_{3}+\cdots+\alpha_{d_{k}}y_{d_{k}}, where αi\alpha_{i} is an element of ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}} for each i∈{1,2,…,dk}i\in\{1,2,\ldots,d_{k}\}. Then one verifies easily from the definition of φ\varphi that for n∈ℤ∖{0}n\in\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}

(φn)+​(α1​y1+y2+α3​y3+⋯+αdk​ydk)=(α1+n)​y1+y2+α3​y3+⋯+αdk​ydk∉k+(d=1).\displaystyle(\varphi^{n})_{+}(\alpha_{1}y_{1}+y_{2}+\alpha_{3}y_{3}+\cdots+\alpha_{d_{k}}y_{d_{k}})=(\alpha_{1}+n)y_{1}+y_{2}+\alpha_{3}y_{3}+\cdots+\alpha_{d_{k}}y_{d_{k}}\notin k^{(d=1)}_{+}.

This completes the proof of assertion (1).

Next, we verify assertion (2). Since 𝒪k(d=1)×\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times} is a profinite group, to show that the subgroup φ×​(𝒪k(d=1)×)∩𝒪k(d=1)×⊂𝒪k(d=1)×\varphi^{\times}(\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times})\cap\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}\subset\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times} is not open in 𝒪k(d=1)×\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}, it suffices to show that it is not a subgroup of finite index. Moreover, it follows from [Hsh3], Lemma 1.2, (i)\rm(\hskip 1.79993pti\hskip 1.79993pt), (iv)\rm(i\hskip-0.80002ptv\hskip-0.59998pt), and the definition of perfection [cf. §0, Notational conventions, Monoids] that it suffices to show φ+​(k+(d=1))∩k+(d=1)=0\varphi_{+}(k^{(d=1)}_{+})\cap k^{(d=1)}_{+}=0 in order to prove that the subgroup

φ×​(𝒪k(d=1)×)∩𝒪k(d=1)×⊂𝒪k(d=1)×\displaystyle\varphi^{\times}(\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times})\cap\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}\subset\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}

is not of finite index. It immediately follows from assertion (1) and the fact that the subspace k+(d=1)k_{+}^{(d=1)} is a one-dimensional ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}-vector space. Thus, the subgroup φ×​(𝒪k(d=1)×)∩𝒪k(d=1)×\varphi^{\times}(\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times})\cap\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times} is not of finite index in 𝒪k(d=1)×\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}. This completes the proof of assertion (2). ∎

Definition 1.6.

We shall say that the MLF kk is an absolutely Galois MLF if the extension k/k(d=1)k/k^{(d=1)} is a Galois extension.

Definition 1.7.

Let VV be a ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}-vector space of finite dimension and ρ:Gk→Autℚpk⁡(V)\rho\colon G_{k}\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(V) a continuous representation. Then we shall say that ρ\rho is Aut-intrinsically Hodge-Tate if, for an arbitrary [continuous] automorphism α\alpha of GkG_{k}, the composite ρ∘α:Gk→Autℚpk⁡(V)\rho\circ\alpha\colon G_{k}\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(V) is Hodge-Tate.

Definition 1.8.

Suppose that kk is an absolutely Galois MLF. Let π∈𝒪k\pi\in\mathcal{O}_{k} be a uniformizer of 𝒪k\mathcal{O}_{k} and σ\sigma an element of Gal⁡(k/k(d=1))\Gal(k/k^{(d=1)}). Then we shall write

χπ,σ:Gkab→reck−1k×^↠𝒪k×→σ𝒪k×,\displaystyle\chi_{\pi,\sigma}\colon G_{k}^{\ab}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\rec_{k}^{-1}}}{{\to}}\widehat{k^{\times}}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sigma}}{{\to}}\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times},

where the second arrow is the projection determined by π\pi.

With the above preparations, we now prove the first main theorem of the present paper.

Theorem 1.9.

Suppose that pkp_{k} is odd, that dkd_{k} is even, and that kk is an absolutely Galois MLF. Then there exist a ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}-vector space VV of dimension dkd_{k}, a continuous representation ρ:Gk→Autℚpk⁡(V)\rho\colon G_{k}\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(V) that is irreducible, abelian, and crystalline [hence also Hodge-Tate], but not Aut-intrinsically Hodge-Tate.

Proof.

Let π∈𝒪k\pi\in\mathcal{O}_{k} be a uniformizer of 𝒪k\mathcal{O}_{k}. We write ρ\rho for the continuous representation of GkG_{k} [necessarily of dimension dkd_{k}] obtained by forming the composite

Gk↠Gkab→χπ,idk𝒪k×↪Autℚpk⁡(k+),\displaystyle G_{k}\twoheadrightarrow G_{k}^{\ab}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\chi_{\pi,\id_{k}}}}{{\to}}\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times}\hookrightarrow\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(k_{+}),

where the first arrow is the natural surjective continuous homomorphism, and the third arrow is the natural inclusion. Then one verifies easily that this continuous representation ρ\rho is irreducible and abelian.

Next, we show that ρ\rho is a crystalline representation. Let FπF_{\pi} be the Lubin-Tate formal group law associated with the Lubin-Tate formal power series π​t+tpkfk\pi t+t^{{p_{k}}^{f_{k}}}. Then ρ\rho is isomorphic to the continuous pkp_{k}-adic representation induced by the action on the pkp_{k}-adic Tate module of FπF_{\pi} [cf., e.g., [Ser], III\rm I\hskip-1.49994ptI\hskip-1.49994ptI, §A.4, Proposition 4]. Since FπF_{\pi} is defined over 𝒪k\mathcal{O}_{k}, the corresponding pkp_{k}-divisible group is also defined over 𝒪k\mathcal{O}_{k}. It is well-known [cf. [Fon], Theorem 6.2, OPENi)\rm\hskip 1.79993pti\hskip 1.79993pt)] that the continuous pkp_{k}-adic representation induced by the action on the pkp_{k}-adic Tate module of FπF_{\pi} is crystalline. Thus, the representation ρ\rho is a crystalline representation.

Next, we show by contradiction that the continuous representation ρ∘φ\rho\circ\varphi is not Hodge–Tate, where φ\varphi is the automorphism of GkG_{k} defined in the statement of Lemma 1.5. Let us recall that it follows immediately from the various definitions involved that the composite

𝒪k×↪reckGkab→χπ,idk𝒪k×\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\rec_{k}}}{{\hookrightarrow}}G_{k}^{\ab}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\chi_{\pi,\id_{k}}}}{{\to}}\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times}

is an automorphism that restricts to an automorphism of the subgroup 𝒪k(d=1)×⊂𝒪k×\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}\subset\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times}. We write φab:Gkab⟶∼Gkab\varphi^{\ab}\colon G_{k}^{\ab}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{k}^{\ab} for the automorphism of the topological group GkabG_{k}^{\ab} induced by φ\varphi. It follows from the assumption of the contradiction that ρ∘φ\rho\circ\varphi is Hodge–Tate. Thus, it follows from [Hsh4], Lemma 1.9, that there exists an open subgroup U⊂𝒪k(d=1)×U\subset\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times} whose image by the composite

𝒪k(d=1)×↪𝒪k×↪Gkab→𝒪k×,\displaystyle\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}\hookrightarrow\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times}\hookrightarrow G_{k}^{\ab}\to\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times},

where the first arrow is a natural injective homomorphism, the second arrow is the injective homomorphism obtained by restricting the local reciprocity homomorphism of kk, and the third arrow is χπ,idk∘φab\chi_{\pi,\id_{k}}\circ\varphi^{\ab}, is contained in the subgroup 𝒪k(d=1)×⊂𝒪k×\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}\subset\mathcal{O}_{k}^{\times}. Thus, it follows from the various definitions involved that φ×​(U)⊂𝒪k(d=1)×\varphi^{\times}(U)\subset\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times} and is an open subgroup of 𝒪k(d=1)×\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}. In particular, we obtain that φ×​(U)⊂φ×​(𝒪k(d=1)×)∩𝒪k(d=1)×\varphi^{\times}(U)\subset\varphi^{\times}(\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times})\cap\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}. However, this contradicts Lemma 1.5, (2), since φ×​(U)⊂𝒪k(d=1)×\varphi^{\times}(U)\subset\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times} is an open subgroup of 𝒪k(d=1)×\mathcal{O}_{k^{(d=1)}}^{\times}. Thus, the composite ρ∘φ:Gk→Autℚpk⁡(k+)\rho\circ\varphi\colon G_{k}\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(k_{+}) is not Hodge-Tate. This completes the proof of Theorem 1.9. ∎

Remark 1.10.

In the case where dkd_{k} is odd, a proof analogous to that of Theorem 1.9 would require an element α∈Aut⁡(Gk)\alpha\in\Aut(G_{k}) such that α+​(y1)≠y1\alpha_{+}(y_{1})\neq y_{1}. However, at the time of writing, it is not clear to the author whether or not such an element exists. For this reason, the assumption that dkd_{k} is even is imposed in Theorem 1.9.

Remark 1.11.

Suppose that dk=1d_{k}=1 and that pkp_{k} is odd. As observed in the proof of Theorem 1.9, there exists an irreducible, abelian, and crystalline [hence, Hodge-Tate] one-dimensional continuous representation ρ0:Gk→Autℚpk⁡(V)\rho_{0}\colon G_{k}\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(V). As shown in [Hsh4], Theorem A, when a continuous pkp_{k}-adic representation ρ:Gk→Autℚpk⁡(V)\rho\colon G_{k}\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(V) is one-dimensional, or, even, two-dimensional and reducible, the property that ρ\rho is Hodge-Tate is equivalent to the property that ρ\rho is Aut-intrinsically Hodge-Tate. Thus, this representation ρ0:Gk→Autℚpk⁡(V)\rho_{0}\colon G_{k}\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(V) is Aut-intrinsically Hodge-Tate.

On the other hand, it is well-known [cf., e.g., the discussion given at the final portion of [N-S-W], Chapter VII, §5] that there exists an outer automorphism of GkG_{k} that is not induced by any field automorphism of kk. Thus, it follows from [Hsh1], Corollary 3.4, that there exists a continuous representation of GkG_{k} that is Hodge-Tate but not Aut-intrinsically Hodge-Tate. It follows that the following inclusion holds:

∅≠{Aut-intrinsically Hodge-Tate}⊊{Hodge-Tate}.\displaystyle\emptyset\neq\{\text{Aut-intrinsically Hodge-Tate}\}\subsetneq\{\text{Hodge-Tate}\}.
Remark 1.12.

Let χ:Gk→ℚpk×\chi\colon G_{k}\to\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}^{\times} be a nontrivial continuous character which factors through Gal⁡(K/k)\Gal(K/k) for some totally ramified finite extension K/kK/k of degree greater than one. Then we observe that the representation ρ′\rho^{\prime} defined by χ\chi is de Rham [hence also Hodge-Tate] but not crystalline as follows. In fact, the de Rham-ness of ρ′\rho^{\prime} follows from the facts that a continuous pkp_{k}-adic representation is de Rham if and only if its restriction to an open subgroup is de Rham, together with the fact that the trivial representation is de Rham. Next, we show that the representation ρ′\rho^{\prime} is not crystalline. Let us write GK=defGal⁡(k¯/K)G_{K}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\Gal(\overline{k}/K) for the absolute Galois group of KK determined by k¯\overline{k}. Since K/kK/k is a totally ramified extension, we have BcrisGK≅k0B_{\mathrm{cris}}^{G_{K}}\cong k_{0}, where BcrisB_{\mathrm{cris}} denotes the crystalline period ring, and k0k_{0} is the maximal unramified subextension of k/k(d=1)k/k^{(d=1)}. Moreover, by the definition of χ\chi, we have ℚpk​(χ)GK=ℚpk​(χ)\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}(\chi)^{G_{K}}=\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}(\chi) and ℚpk​(χ)Gal⁡(K/k)=0\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}(\chi)^{\Gal(K/k)}=0, where ℚpk​(χ)\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}(\chi) denotes the ℚpk​[Gk]\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[G_{k}]-module whose underlying ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}-vector space is ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}} and on which GkG_{k} acts via χ\chi. Thus, we have

(ℚpk​(χ)⊗ℚpkBcris)Gk≅\displaystyle(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}(\chi)\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}B_{\mathrm{cris}})^{G_{k}}\cong ((ℚpk​(χ)⊗ℚpkBcris)GK)Gal⁡(K/k)≅(ℚpk​(χ)⊗ℚpkk0)Gal⁡(K/k)=0.\displaystyle((\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}(\chi)\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}B_{\mathrm{cris}})^{G_{K}})^{\Gal(K/k)}\cong(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}(\chi)\otimes_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}k_{0})^{\Gal(K/k)}=0.

In particular, the representation ρ′\rho^{\prime} is not crystalline.

We note that any one-dimensional continuous linear representation that is Hodge-Tate is necessarily Aut-intrinsically Hodge-Tate [cf. [Hsh4], Theorem A]. In particular, the representation ρ′\rho^{\prime} is Aut-intrinsically Hodge-Tate but not crystalline. Thus, there is no inclusion relation in either direction between the classes of Aut-intrinsically Hodge-Tate representations and crystalline representations.

Remark 1.13.

An interesting problem related to Aut-intrinsic Hodge-Tate-ness is whether, given an automorphism α:Gk⟶∼Gk\alpha\colon G_{k}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{k}, one can suitably formulate, by means of α\alpha, the difference between the class of continuous representations of GkG_{k} that are Hodge-Tate and the class of continuous representations of GkG_{k} that are Hodge-Tate but cease to be so after composition with α\alpha. However, at the time of writing the present paper, this problem remains unexplored.

2 On the non-normality of the field-theoretic subgroups of the outer automorphism groups of the absolute Galois groups of absolutely Galois MLFs

In the present §2, let kk be an MLF, k¯\overline{k} an algebraic closure of kk, and GG a group of MLF-type. In the present §2, we discuss the outer automorphism groups of the absolute Galois groups of certain MLFs. In particular, we show that if pkp_{k} is odd, dkd_{k} is greater than one, and kk is an absolutely Galois MLF, i.e., the extension k/k(d=1)k/k^{(d=1)} is a Galois extension, then the field-theoretic subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is not normal. This result generalizes certain theorems in [H-N] and [Hsh2].

Definition 2.1.

We shall refer to the image of the natural injective group homomorphism Aut⁡(k)↪Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\hookrightarrow\Out(G_{k}) [cf., e.g., [Hsh3], Proposition 2.1] as the field-theoretic subgroup of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}).

Remark 2.2.

It is well-known that the isomorphism class of the field kk itself cannot be reconstructed group-theoretically from GkG_{k} in general. For example, let pp be an odd prime number, k0=defℚp​(ζp,pp)k_{0}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\mathbb{Q}_{p}(\zeta_{p},\sqrt[p]{p}) and k1=defℚp​(ζp,p+1p)k_{1}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\mathbb{Q}_{p}(\zeta_{p},\sqrt[p]{p+1}), where ζp\zeta_{p} is a primitive pp-th root of unity. Fix an algebraic closure k0¯\overline{k_{0}} of k0k_{0} and an algebraic closure k1¯\overline{k_{1}} of k1k_{1}. Then it follows from the main theorem of [J-R] that the group Gk0=defGal⁡(k0¯/k0)G_{k_{0}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\Gal(\overline{k_{0}}/k_{0}) is isomorphic to the group Gk1=defGal⁡(k1¯/k1)G_{k_{1}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\Gal(\overline{k_{1}}/k_{1}), while the field k0k_{0} is not isomorphic to the field k1k_{1}.

Furthermore, the following observation illustrates, in a stronger sense, that a group isomorphism Gk0≅Gk1G_{k_{0}}\cong G_{k_{1}} is not compatible with their ring structures. Let φ:Gk1⟶∼Gk0\varphi\colon G_{k_{1}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{k_{0}} be an arbitrary group isomorphism, and let Φ:Out⁡(Gk1)⟶∼Out⁡(Gk0)\Phi\colon\Out(G_{k_{1}})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Out(G_{k_{0}}) denote the induced group isomorphism. Then it follows from [Hsh2], Corollary 8.6, that Φ⁡(Gal⁡(k1/ℚp​(ζp)))⊄NOut⁡(Gk0)​(Aut⁡(k0))\Phi(\Gal(k_{1}/\mathbb{Q}_{p}(\zeta_{p})))\not\subset N_{\Out(G_{k_{0}})}(\Aut(k_{0})). In particular, the subgroup Aut⁡(k0)⊂Out⁡(Gk0)\Aut(k_{0})\subset\Out(G_{k_{0}}) is not a normal subgroup of Out⁡(Gk0)\Out(G_{k_{0}}).

It follows from Lemma 1.5, (2), that there exists an outer automorphism α∈Out⁡(Gk)\alpha\in\Out(G_{k}) such that the automorphism α×:k×⟶∼k×\alpha^{\times}\colon k^{\times}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}k^{\times} induced by the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm does not preserve the subgroup (k(d=1))×⊂k×(k^{(d=1)})^{\times}\subset k^{\times}. In particular, the subgroup (k(d=1))×⊂k×(k^{(d=1)})^{\times}\subset k^{\times} cannot be reconstructed group-theoretically and functorially from the group GkG_{k} in general. However, we will show that if kk is absolutely Galois and α∈NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))\alpha\in N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)), then the induced isomorphism α×\alpha^{\times} preserves the subgroup (k(d=1))×⊂k×(k^{(d=1)})^{\times}\subset k^{\times} [cf. Theorem 2.8 below].

Definition 2.3.

Let Π\Pi be a profinite group. Then we shall say that Π\Pi is slim if for every open subgroup Γ\Gamma of Π\Pi, the equality ZΠ​(Γ)=1Z_{\Pi}(\Gamma)={1} holds.

A group of MLF-type is an example of a slim profinite group [cf., e.g., [Hsh3], Proposition 1.8].

Lemma 2.4.

Let Π\Pi be a slim profinite group, and let Γ⊂Π\Gamma\subset\Pi be an open normal subgroup of Π\Pi. We write AutΓ⁡(Π)\Aut_{\Gamma}(\Pi) for the subgroup of Aut⁡(Π)\Aut(\Pi) consisting of elements φ\varphi such that φ⁡(Γ)=Γ\varphi(\Gamma)=\Gamma. Then the following assertions hold:

  1. (1)

    The restriction map

    is an injective group homomorphism.

  2. (2)

    The outer action Π/Γ→Out⁡(Γ)\Pi/\Gamma\to\Out(\Gamma), which is defined by the natural exact sequence of groups

    1→Γ→Π→Π/Γ→1,\displaystyle 1\to\Gamma\to\Pi\to\Pi/\Gamma\to 1,

    is injective.

  3. (3)

    We regard Π/Γ\Pi/\Gamma as a subgroup of Out⁡(Γ)\Out(\Gamma) via the outer action Π/Γ↪Out⁡(Γ)\Pi/\Gamma\hookrightarrow\Out(\Gamma) [cf. assertion (2)] and AutΓ⁡(Π)/Inn⁡(Γ)\Aut_{\Gamma}(\Pi)/\Inn(\Gamma) as a subgroup of Out⁡(Γ)\Out(\Gamma) via the natural injection AutΓ⁡(Π)/Inn⁡(Γ)↪Out⁡(Γ)\Aut_{\Gamma}(\Pi)/\Inn(\Gamma)\hookrightarrow\Out(\Gamma) [cf. assertion (1)]. Then the following equality holds:

    NOut⁡(Γ)​(Π/Γ)=AutΓ⁡(Π)/Inn⁡(Γ).\displaystyle N_{\Out(\Gamma)}(\Pi/\Gamma)=\Aut_{\Gamma}(\Pi)/\Inn(\Gamma).
Proof.

First, we verify assertion (1). Let φ∈AutΓ⁡(Π)\varphi\in\Aut_{\Gamma}(\Pi). Since Π\Pi is slim, the group homomorphism Π→Aut⁡(Γ)\Pi\to\Aut(\Gamma) by conjugation is injective. Moreover, it follows from various definitions involved that the following diagram commutes:

where the right-hand vertical arrow is the group homomorphism given conjugation by φ|Γ\varphi|_{\Gamma}. Thus, if φ|Γ=idΓ\varphi|_{\Gamma}=\id_{\Gamma}, then it follows from the commutativity of this diagram and the injectivity of Π→Aut⁡(Γ)\Pi\to\Aut(\Gamma) that φ=idΠ\varphi=\id_{\Pi}. This completes the proof of assertion (1).

Next, we verify assertion (2). Let π∈Π\pi\in\Pi be an element. We write iπi_{\pi} for the inner automorphism of Π\Pi determined by π\pi. Suppose that the automorphism iπ|Γi_{\pi}|_{\Gamma} of Γ\Gamma is an inner automorphism. Then there exists an element γ0∈Γ\gamma_{0}\in\Gamma such that iπ|Γ=iγ0|Γi_{\pi}|_{\Gamma}=i_{\gamma_{0}}|_{\Gamma}, where iγ0i_{\gamma_{0}} denotes the inner automorphism of Π\Pi determined by γ0\gamma_{0}. Thus, it follows from the slimness of Π\Pi and the injectivity of the map AutΓ⁡(Π)→Aut⁡(Γ)\Aut_{\Gamma}(\Pi)\to\Aut(\Gamma), φ↦φ|Γ\varphi\mapsto\varphi|_{\Gamma} [cf. assertion (1)], that π=γ0∈Γ\pi=\gamma_{0}\in\Gamma. This completes the proof of assertion (2).

Next, we verify assertion (3). Since Π\Pi is slim, and slimness is inherited by open subgroups, it follows that Γ\Gamma is also slim. In particular, the injection Π/Γ↪Out⁡(Γ)\Pi/\Gamma\hookrightarrow\Out(\Gamma) of assertion (2) splits as the isomorphism Π/Γ⟶∼Inn⁡(Π)/Inn⁡(Γ)\Pi/\Gamma\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Inn(\Pi)/\Inn(\Gamma) and the inclusion Inn⁡(Π)/Inn⁡(Γ)↪Out⁡(Γ)\Inn(\Pi)/\Inn(\Gamma)\hookrightarrow\Out(\Gamma). Thus, it is immediate that, to verify assertion (3), it suffices to show that NAut⁡(Γ)​(Inn⁡(Π))=AutΓ⁡(Π)N_{\Aut(\Gamma)}(\Inn(\Pi))=\Aut_{\Gamma}(\Pi). The inclusion AutΓ⁡(Π)⊂NAut⁡(Γ)​(Inn⁡(Π))\Aut_{\Gamma}(\Pi)\subset N_{\Aut(\Gamma)}(\Inn(\Pi)) is trivial.

We now show the inclusion NAut⁡(Γ)​(Inn⁡(Π))⊂AutΓ⁡(Π)N_{\Aut(\Gamma)}(\Inn(\Pi))\subset\Aut_{\Gamma}(\Pi). Take an element φ∈NAut⁡(Γ)​(Inn⁡(Π))\varphi\in N_{\Aut(\Gamma)}(\Inn(\Pi)). For each element π∈Π\pi\in\Pi, there exists π′∈Π\pi^{\prime}\in\Pi such that the following equality holds:

φ∘(iπ|Γ)∘φ−1=iπ′|Γ,\displaystyle\varphi\circ(i_{\pi}|_{\Gamma})\circ\varphi^{-1}=i_{\pi^{\prime}}|_{\Gamma},

where we write iπi_{\pi}, iπ′i_{\pi^{\prime}} for the inner automorphisms of Π\Pi determined by π\pi, π′\pi^{\prime} respectively. Since Γ\Gamma is slim, the element π′\pi^{\prime} is uniquely determined by π\pi. Moreover, it is easy to verify that if π∈Γ\pi\in\Gamma, then π′=φ⁡(π)\pi^{\prime}=\varphi(\pi). Furthermore, it is also easy to verify that if we define the map ψ:Π→Π\psi\colon\Pi\to\Pi by ψ⁡(π)=defπ′\psi(\pi)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\pi^{\prime}, then ψ\psi is an automorphism of Π\Pi that satisfies ψ|Γ=φ\psi|_{\Gamma}=\varphi. Theorem 2.8.

Let α\alpha be an element of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}). Suppose that kk is an absolutely Galois MLF. If α∈NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))\alpha\in N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)), then α\alpha is ℚpk×\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}^{\times}-preserving.

Proof.

This assertion follows immediately from Proposition 2.5, (3), Lemma 2.7, the commutative diagram appearing in the statement of [Hsh3], Lemma 1.7, (iii)\rm(i\hskip-0.80002pti\hskip-0.80002pti), and the functoriality of the transfer map. ∎

The second main theorem of the present paper — namely, the non-normality of the field-theoretic subgroup of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) — follows from some results in §1 and the techniques developed in [H-N] under the assumptions that dkd_{k} is even, pkp_{k} is odd, and kk is absolutely Galois.

Theorem 2.9.

Suppose that kk is an absolutely Galois MLF, that pkp_{k} is odd, and that dkd_{k} is even. Then the set of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k})-conjugates of the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is infinite. In particular, the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is not a normal subgroup of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}).

Proof.

Let φ\varphi be the automorphism of GkG_{k} defined in the statement of Lemma 1.5. Then it follows from Theorem 2.8, and Lemma 1.5, (2), that φn∉NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))\varphi^{n}\notin N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)) for all integer n≠0n\neq 0. In particular, the set of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k})-conjugates of the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is infinite. ∎

Remark 2.10.

Theorem 2.9 is a generalization of the main theorem of [H-N] and one of the main results of [Hsh2], which appeared in Remark 2.2. The method of the proof of Theorem 2.9 is essentially the same as the method of the proof that was applied in [H-N] and is substantially different from the approach taken in [Hsh2].

Remark 2.11.

Suppose that the subgroup Gk⊂Gk(d=1)G_{k}\subset G_{k^{(d=1)}} is a characteristic open subgroup. For example, if k/k(d=1)k/k^{(d=1)} is an abelian extension, then the subgroup Gk⊂Gk(d=1)G_{k}\subset G_{k^{(d=1)}} is characteristic and open [cf. [Hsh2], Theorem 6.3, (i)\rm(\hskip 1.79993pti\hskip 1.79993pt)]. Then, by Proposition 2.5, (2), (3), we obtain the following exact sequence of groups:

1→Aut⁡(k)→NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))→Out⁡(Gk(d=1))→1.\displaystyle 1\to\Aut(k)\to N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))\to\Out(G_{k^{(d=1)}})\to 1.

From the existence of this exact sequence and the fact that Out⁡(Gk(d=1))≠1\Out(G_{k^{(d=1)}})\neq 1 for odd residue characteristic pkp_{k} [cf., e.g., the discussion given at the final portion of [N-S-W], Chapter VII, §5], we deduce that Aut⁡(k)⊊NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))\Aut(k)\subsetneq N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)). Put another way, there exists an element α∈NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))\alpha\in N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)) such that α∉Aut⁡(k)\alpha\notin\Aut(k). As discussed in the discussion following Remark 2.2, in general, the subgroup (k(d=1))×⊂k×(k^{(d=1)})^{\times}\subset k^{\times} cannot be reconstructed from the group GkG_{k} in a purely group-theoretic and functorial manner. Put another way, the subgroup (k(d=1))×⊂k×(k^{(d=1)})^{\times}\subset k^{\times} depends on the ring structure of kk in an essential way. On the other hand, by Theorem 2.8, if kk is an absolutely Galois MLF and α∈NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))\alpha\in N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)), then the induced isomorphism α×\alpha^{\times} preserves the subgroup (k(d=1))×⊂k×(k^{(d=1)})^{\times}\subset k^{\times} and α×|(k(d=1))×=id(k(d=1))×\alpha^{\times}|_{(k^{(d=1)})^{\times}}=\id_{(k^{(d=1)})^{\times}}. It follows from this discussion that every element α∈NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))\alpha\in N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)), which is not necessarily contained in Aut⁡(k)\Aut(k), preserves certain structures of ring-theoretic nature.

We now prepare to prove the non-normality of the field-theoretic subgroup of the outer automorphism group of the absolute Galois group of kk in the case where dkd_{k} is odd, kk is absolutely Galois, and pkp_{k} is odd.

In the remainder of the present paper, we assume that the prime numbers pkp_{k} and p⁡(G)p(G) are odd.

Since GG is a topologically finitely generated profinite group [cf. Theorem 1.1], for any integer n>0n>0, there exist only finitely many subgroups of GG of index nn. In particular, the set of all characteristic subgroups of GG of finite index forms a fundamental system of open neighborhoods of 1∈G1\in G. Hence, it follows from [R-Z], Proposition 4.4.3, that Aut⁡(G)\Aut(G) and Out⁡(G)\Out(G) have natural profinite group structures. In the remainder of the present paper, we endow Aut⁡(G)\Aut(G) and Out⁡(G)\Out(G) with these profinite group structures.

Let us consider the group homomorphism Out⁡(G)→Autℚp⁡(G)⁡(k+​(G))\Out(G)\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}}(k_{+}(G)) defined via the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm [cf. [Hsh3], Proposition 3.11, (iv)\rm(i\hskip-0.80002ptv\hskip-0.59998pt), [H-N], Lemma 1.2]. We equip Autℚp⁡(G)⁡(k+​(G))\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}}(k_{+}(G)) with the topology induced by the p⁡(G)p(G)-adic topology of k+​(G)k_{+}(G), i.e., the relative topology with respect to

Autℚp⁡(G)⁡(k+​(G))⊂Endℚp⁡(G)⁡(k+​(G))≅ℚp⁡(G)d​(G)2,\displaystyle\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}}(k_{+}(G))\subset\End_{\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}}(k_{+}(G))\cong\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}^{d(G)^{2}},

or, equivalently, the compact open topology defined by the p⁡(G)p(G)-adic topology of k+​(G)k_{+}(G).

Lemma 2.13.

The action Aut​(G)↷k+​(G)\mathrm{Aut}(G)\curvearrowright k_{+}(G) which is defined via the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm is continuous. In particular, the induced maps Aut⁡(G)→Autℚp⁡(G)⁡(k+​(G))\Aut(G)\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}}(k_{+}(G)) and Out⁡(G)→Autℚp⁡(G)⁡(k+​(G))\Out(G)\to\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}}(k_{+}(G)) are continuous and closed.

Proof.

Since k+​(G)k_{+}(G) is a locally compact Hausdorff space, the topological spaces Aut⁡(G)\Aut(G) and Out⁡(G)\Out(G) are compact, and Autℚp⁡(G)⁡(k+​(G))\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p(G)}}(k_{+}(G)) is Hausdorff, to verify Lemma 2.13, it suffices to show that the action Aut​(G)↷k+​(G)\mathrm{Aut}(G)\curvearrowright k_{+}(G) defined via the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm is continuous. Moreover, since the map Aut⁡(𝒪×​(G))→Aut⁡(k+​(G))\Aut(\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G))\to\Aut(k_{+}(G)) induced by the functoriality of perfection [cf. §0, Notational conventions, Monoids] is continuous with respect to the compact-open topology on Aut⁡(𝒪×​(G))\Aut(\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)), to verify Lemma 2.13, it suffices to show that the action Aut⁡(G)↷𝒪×​(G)\Aut(G)\curvearrowright\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G) defined via the mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm is continuous.

By construction, the map Aut⁡(G)→Aut⁡(𝒪×​(G))\Aut(G)\to\Aut(\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)) factors through the composite Aut⁡(G)→Aut𝒪×​(G)⁡(Gab)→Aut⁡(𝒪×​(G))\Aut(G)\to\Aut_{\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)}(G^{\mathrm{ab}})\to\Aut(\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)), where we write Aut𝒪×​(G)⁡(Gab)\Aut_{\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)}(G^{\mathrm{ab}}) for the subgroup of Aut⁡(Gab)\Aut(G^{\mathrm{ab}}) consisting of elements that preserve the subgroup 𝒪×​(G)⊂Gab\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)\subset G^{\mathrm{ab}}. We equip Aut⁡(Gab)\Aut(G^{\mathrm{ab}}) with the profinite topology as in the case of Aut⁡(G)\Aut(G). The subgroup Aut𝒪×​(G)⁡(Gab)\Aut_{\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)}(G^{\mathrm{ab}}) is endowed with the subspace topology induced from Aut⁡(Gab)\Aut(G^{\mathrm{ab}}). It is clear that the map Aut⁡(G)→Aut𝒪×​(G)⁡(Gab)\Aut(G)\to\Aut_{\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)}(G^{\mathrm{ab}}) is continuous. Moreover, since the profinite topology and the compact-open topology on Aut⁡(Gab)\mathrm{Aut}(G^{\mathrm{ab}}) coincide [cf., e.g., [R-Z], Theorem 4.4.2], the map Aut𝒪×​(G)⁡(Gab)→Aut⁡(𝒪×​(G))\Aut_{\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)}(G^{\mathrm{ab}})\to\Aut(\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)), which is defined by φ↦φ|𝒪×​(G)\varphi\mapsto\varphi|_{\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G)}, is continuous. Thus, the action Aut⁡(G)↷𝒪×​(G)\Aut(G)\curvearrowright\mathcal{O}^{\times}(G) is continuous. This completes the proof of Lemma 2.13. ∎

When dk>1d_{k}>1, let us consider the basis y1,…,ydky_{1},\ldots,y_{d_{k}} of k+k_{+} over ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}} corresponding to the basis of k+​(Gk)k_{+}(G_{k}) that appeared in the discussion preceding Lemma 1.2 via the isomorphism of topological groups k+​(Gk)⟶∼k+k_{+}(G_{k})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}k_{+} of [Hsh3], Proposition 3.11, (iv)\rm(i\hskip-0.80002ptv\hskip-0.59998pt). Lemma 2.14.

Suppose that kk is an absolutely Galois MLF and that dk>1d_{k}>1. Then the following assertions hold:

  1. (1)

    The centralizer of H=defAut⁡(k)⊂Autℚpk⁡(k+)=GLdk⁡(ℚpk)H\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\Aut(k)\subset\Aut_{\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}}(k_{+})=\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}) in GLdk⁡(ℚpk)\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}) is a closed subgroup of GLdk⁡(ℚpk)\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}).     ZGLdk⁡(ℚpk)​(H)⟶∼(ℚpk​[H])×.\displaystyle Z_{\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}})}(H)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[H])^{\times}.

    The dimension of the pkp_{k}-adic Lie group ZGLdk⁡(ℚpk)​(H)Z_{\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}})}(H) is at most dkd_{k}.

Since H=Aut⁡(k)H=\Aut(k) is a finite group, assertion (1) holds. Next, we verify assertion (2). Since kk is absolutely Galois and H=Aut⁡(k)=Gal⁡(k/k(d=1))H=\Aut(k)=\Gal(k/k^{(d=1)}), it follows from the normal basis theorem that k+≅ℚpk​[H]k_{+}\cong\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[H] as a left ℚpk​[H]\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[H]-module [where k+k_{+} is endowed with its natural left ℚpk​[H]\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[H]-module structure]. By taking the automorphism groups of both sides of the ℚpk\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}-isomorphism k+≅ℚpk​[H]k_{+}\cong\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[H], we obtain a topological group isomorphism

ZGLdk⁡(ℚpk)​(H)⟶∼((ℚpk​[H])×)op⟶∼(ℚpk​[H])×,\displaystyle Z_{\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}})}(H)\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}((\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[H])^{\times})^{\mathrm{op}}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[H])^{\times},

where we note that the centralizer ZGLdk⁡(ℚpk)​(H)Z_{\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}})}(H) is naturally isomorphic to the group of automorphisms of k+k_{+} as a left ℚpk​[H]\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[H]-module. By construction, this isomorphism is compatible with the natural pkp_{k}-adic Lie group structure and thus gives an isomorphism of pkp_{k}-adic Lie groups. This completes the proof of assertion (2). Finally, since the dimension of (ℚpk​[H])×(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[H])^{\times} as a pkp_{k}-adic Lie group is at most dkd_{k}, it follows from assertion (2) that assertion (3) holds. This completes the proof of Lemma 2.14. ∎

Lemma 2.15.

Let nn be a positive integer. Then the group Sp2​n​(ℤpk)\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{Z}_{p_{k}}) is not a virtually abelian profinite group, i.e., has no abelian open subgroup.

Proof.

Let UU be an open subgroup of Sp2​n​(ℤpk)\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{Z}_{p_{k}}). Since Sp2​n​(ℤpk)\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{Z}_{p_{k}}) is a compact open subgroup of the pkp_{k}-adic Lie group Sp2​n​(ℚpk)\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}), it naturally carries a structure of pkp_{k}-adic Lie group and, in particular, is profinite. In general, for a pkp_{k}-adic Lie group XX, the Lie algebra structure defined on the tangent space at the identity element of XX is naturally identified with the Lie algebra structure defined on the tangent space at the identity element of any open subgroup of XX. Thus, the Lie algebra associated with Sp2​n​(ℤpk)\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{Z}_{p_{k}}) is naturally identified with the Lie algebra associated with UU. We prove Lemma 2.15 by contradiction. Suppose that UU is abelian. Then the Lie bracket on the corresponding Lie algebra is trivial. However, this contradicts the fact that the Lie bracket on the Lie algebra 𝔰​𝔭2​n​(ℚpk)\mathfrak{sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}), which is associated with Sp2​n​(ℤpk)\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(\mathbb{Z}_{p_{k}}), is nontrivial. This completes the proof of Lemma 2.15. ∎

Theorem 2.19.

Suppose that kk is an absolutely Galois MLF, that pkp_{k} is odd, and that dk>1d_{k}>1 is odd. Then the set of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k})-conjugates of the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is infinite. In particular, Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is not a normal subgroup of Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}).

Proof.

It follows from the existence of the natural exact sequence

1→ZOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))→NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))→Aut⁡(Aut⁡(k)),\displaystyle 1\to Z_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))\to N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))\to\Aut(\Aut(k)),

together with the fact that Aut⁡(k)\Aut(k) is a finite group, that the subgroup ZOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))⊂NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))Z_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))\subset N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)) is of finite index. Thus, in order to show that the subgroup

NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))⊂Out⁡(Gk)\displaystyle N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))\subset\Out(G_{k})

is not of finite index, it suffices to show that the subgroup ZOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))⊂Out⁡(Gk)Z_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))\subset\Out(G_{k}) is not of finite index.

We first consider the case where g≥2g\geq 2. It follows from Lemma 2.13 that the map Φ\Phi [cf. Remark 2.18] is a closed map. Thus, both I=defΦ⁡(Out⁡(Gk))I\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\Phi(\Out(G_{k})) and Z=defΦ⁡(ZOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k)))Z\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\mathrm{def}}}{{=}}\Phi(Z_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))) are closed subgroups of GLdk⁡(ℚpk)\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}). In particular, it follows from [D-S-M-S], Theorem 9.6, that both II and ZZ naturally admit structures of pkp_{k}-adic Lie groups. Furthermore, it follows from Remark 2.18 that the image of DD [cf. the discussion preceding Remark 2.16] by Φ\Phi is equal to Sp2​g​(ℤpk)\mathrm{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb{Z}_{p_{k}}), which implies that Sp2​g​(ℤpk)⊂I\mathrm{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb{Z}_{p_{k}})\subset I. As is well-known, since the dimension of Sp2​g​(ℤpk)\mathrm{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb{Z}_{p_{k}}) as a pkp_{k}-adic Lie group is 2​g2+g2g^{2}+g, it follows that dim(I)≥2​g2+g\dim(I)\geq 2g^{2}+g.

Thus, it follows from 2.14, (3), that the dimension of ZGLdk⁡(ℚpk)​(Aut⁡(k))Z_{\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}})}(\Aut(k)) as a pkp_{k}-adic Lie group is at most 2​g+12g+1. Hence, we obtain dim(Z)≤2​g+1\dim(Z)\leq 2g+1. Since g≥2g\geq 2, we have 2​g2+g>2​g+12g^{2}+g>2g+1. Therefore, the dimension comparison shows that ZZ is not an open subgroup of II. Indeed, if ZZ were open in II, then dim(Z)=dim(I)\dim(Z)=\dim(I) would hold, which contradicts the inequality 2​g2+g>2​g+12g^{2}+g>2g+1. On the other hand, since ZZ is a closed subgroup of II [cf. Lemma 2.13], it follows that ZZ is not of finite index in II. In particular, we conclude that the subgroup NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))⊂Out⁡(Gk)N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))\subset\Out(G_{k}) is not of finite index.

Finally, we consider the case where g=1g=1, i.e., dk=3d_{k}=3. Suppose, for the sake of contradiction, that ZOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))⊂Out⁡(Gk)Z_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))\subset\Out(G_{k}) is a subgroup of finite index. Then since the group Aut⁡(k)=Gal⁡(k/k(d=1))\Aut(k)=\Gal(k/k^{(d=1)}) is abelian and ZGLdk⁡(ℚpk)​(Aut⁡(k))≅(ℚpk​[Aut⁡(k)])×Z_{\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}})}(\Aut(k))\cong(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}}[\Aut(k)])^{\times} [cf. Lemma 2.14, (2)], it follows that ZGLdk⁡(ℚpk)​(Aut⁡(k))Z_{\GL_{d_{k}}(\mathbb{Q}_{p_{k}})}(\Aut(k)) is also abelian. Thus, the profinite group II is virtually abelian, i.e., has an abelian open subgroup. Since any closed subgroup of a virtually abelian profinite group is a virtually abelian profinite group, it follows that the closed subgroup Sp2​g​(ℤpk)⊂I\mathrm{Sp}_{2g}(\mathbb{Z}_{p_{k}})\subset I is a virtually abelian profinite group. However, this contradicts Lemma 2.15. This completes the proof of Theorem 2.19. ∎

Remark 2.20.

Suppose that kk is absolutely Galois, that pkp_{k} is odd, and that dk≥2d_{k}\geq 2. Then it follows from Theorem 2.9 and Theorem 2.19 that the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is not normal. Here, we note that this non-normality implies that the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) cannot be reconstructed functorially and group-theoretically from GkG_{k}. Indeed, suppose to the contrary that such a mono-anabelian reconstruction algorithm exists. Then it would imply that, for any automorphism α:Gk⟶∼Gk\alpha\colon G_{k}\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}G_{k} of the group GkG_{k}, we have Out⁡(α)​(Aut⁡(k))=Aut⁡(k)\Out(\alpha)(\Aut(k))=\Aut(k), where we write Out⁡(α):Out⁡(Gk)⟶∼Out⁡(Gk)\Out(\alpha)\colon\Out(G_{k})\stackrel{{\scriptstyle\sim}}{{\longrightarrow}}\Out(G_{k}) for the automorphism of the group Out⁡(Gk)\Out(G_{k}) induced from α\alpha. On the other hand, it follows formally that the automorphism Out⁡(α)\Out(\alpha) coincides with the inner automorphism determined by the image of α\alpha by the natural surjective group homomorphism Aut⁡(Gk)→Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(G_{k})\to\Out(G_{k}). This implies that Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is normal, which contradicts our non-normality result.

Remark 2.21.

Observe that one verifies immediately that the method applied in the proof of Theorem 2.19 [i.e., in the odd degree case] can also be applied to prove Theorem 2.9 [i.e., in the even degree case]. We leave the routine details to the interested reader. On the other hand, in contrast to the proof of Theorem 2.9, the proof of Theorem 2.19 does not enable us to explicitly construct elements of Out⁡(Gk)∖NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))\Out(G_{k})\setminus N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)). That is to say, although its scope is more limited, the method applied in the proof of Theorem 2.9 has the advantage of providing explicit elements of the desired type. Indeed, Theorem 1.9 was obtained through such an observation.

Remark 2.22.

When pk=2p_{k}=2 and −1∈k\sqrt{-1}\in k, as in the case where pkp_{k} is odd, an explicit description by generators and relations for the topological group GkG_{k} [as discussed in Theorem 1.1] is known. In fact, in [Nis], Nishio proved similar results to Theorem 1.9 and Theorem 2.9 in the situation where kk is absolutely abelian, and −1∈k\sqrt{-1}\in k by means of the explicit description. On the other hand, when pk=2p_{k}=2 and −1∉k\sqrt{-1}\notin k, a similar explicit description by generators and relations for the topological group GkG_{k} is not known. In particular, it is not clear to the author at the time of writing whether or not the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is a normal subgroup in the case where pk=2p_{k}=2 and −1∉k\sqrt{-1}\notin k, even when kk is absolutely Galois.

Remark 2.23.

If dk=1d_{k}=1, then it is easy to see that Aut⁡(k)=1\Aut(k)=1. In particular, the subgroup Aut⁡(k)⊂Out⁡(Gk)\Aut(k)\subset\Out(G_{k}) is a normal subgroup. On the other hand, when kk is not absolutely Galois and Aut⁡(k)≠1\Aut(k)\neq 1, the non-normality of the field-theoretic subgroup cannot be established by the method developed in the present paper. In a joint work in preparation by the author and Tsujimura, we are studying similar results to the various results obtained in the present paper under the assumption that Aut⁡(k)≠1\Aut(k)\neq 1 without assuming that kk is absolutely Galois. Moreover, we are also studying analogous results for positive-characteristic local fields and, furthermore, for certain special henselian valued fields that are not necessarily local fields.

Remark 2.24.

Let α∈Out⁡(Gk)\alpha\in\Out(G_{k}). As discussed in Remark 2.11, if α∈NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))\alpha\in N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k)), then it preserves certain objects that essentially depend on the ring structure of kk. On the other hand, by Theorem 2.9 and Theorem 2.19, if kk is absolutely Galois and dk>1d_{k}>1, then the subgroup NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))⊂Out⁡(Gk)N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))\subset\Out(G_{k}) is a proper subgroup. In light of these observations, it is natural to ask whether or not the elements of the subgroup NOut⁡(Gk)​(Aut⁡(k))⊂Out⁡(Gk)N_{\Out(G_{k})}(\Aut(k))\subset\Out(G_{k}) can be characterized, as in Theorem A [cf. Introduction of the present paper], as those that preserve suitable “ring-theoretic data”. However, at the time of writing the present paper, we have not yet obtained even a candidate for an appropriate characterization.
